clue.text: Which material will reportedly make fences?

definitions.text: Which material will reportedly make fences?

parts.words: Which material will reportedly make fences?
parts.note: the clue plays on 'which will' said casually as 'what'll', while asking for a woven fencing material of rods and twigs

explanation.surface: A question about which building material is said to be good for fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which ... will', run together as 'what'll', sounds like the answer, and the answer is also a material woven into fences, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is interwoven stakes and branches, traditionally used to build hurdles and fences.

clue.text: One sings, and you and I pronounce sentence

parts.note: you and I together are we
to aver is to declare or pronounce
bird is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Two people declaring a judgment together.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' for time, is British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaverbird is a songbird that weaves elaborate nests, so it is one that sings.

clue.text: Dressed once and ready for bed

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense, shortened from attired, meaning clothed

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old form meaning clothed, and the everyday adjective for being weary.

clue.text: Misprint ("all rite", possibly?)

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the quoted phrase may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A typing slip shown as an example of mis-spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all rite' is itself an example of a misprint, which makes the clue neat; 'possibly' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a literal is a typographical error, a misprint.

clue.text: Perfect female like Sikes's Nancy?

parts.note: Nancy in Dickens's Oliver Twist is the companion of the criminal Bill Sikes and lives outside the law

explanation.surface: Praising a woman as perfect, in the mould of Dickens's Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy belongs to Fagin's gang of thieves in Oliver Twist, so she is lawless, not perfect: the surface's compliment is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any flaw or blemish is perfect, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Restrict lad's initial announcement when playing tig

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of lad's

parts.note: in tig, the chasing game also called tag, the chaser says 'I'm it'

explanation.surface: A boy calling out during a playground game of chase.
explanation.walkthrough: Tig (tag) is a children's chasing game in which the chaser is 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Travels indirectly round monarch's town

parts.note: something that winds travels a twisting route
a round shape is O
R is the abbreviation for rex or regina, monarch

explanation.surface: A winding route round the royal town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal, but it is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is a town in Berkshire, home of Windsor Castle.

clue.text: European marquis accepts proposal for walk by sea

indicators.note: accepts means the marquis's name takes in the word for proposal

parts.note: the Marquis de Sade, the notorious French aristocrat
a plan is a proposal

explanation.surface: A continental nobleman accepting a marriage proposal on a seaside stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'marquis' is the Marquis de Sade, giving SADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open promenade, especially one along the seafront.

clue.text: Unaccompanied note introducing Beethoven's Sixth

parts.note: sol is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: Sixth picks the sixth letter of Beethoven's

explanation.surface: A lone note opening Beethoven's Pastoral symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Sixth' reads as the symphony, but it means letter six of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo performance is unaccompanied by other players.

clue.text: Best way, say, to produce salad ingredient

indicators.note: say signals the words are to be spoken

parts.note: to best is to beat, and a way is a route

explanation.surface: Asking the best way to prepare a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is the verb (beat), not the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a red root vegetable commonly added to salads.

clue.text: Current way to enter bearing bundle of papers

indicators.note: the word for way is told to go into the two words for bearing and bundle of papers

parts.note: one's bearing is one's air or manner
a ream is a bundle of 500 sheets of paper
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Instructions for routing a delivery of paper bundles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstream is a flow of moving air, a current in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Prickly type turning on mate

indicators.note: turning signals that the little word on is read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A thorny character who turns on a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly type' sounds like a touchy person, but it is a plant: the prickly-pear cactus.
explanation.definitionFit: The nopal is the prickly-pear cactus, a plant covered with spines.

clue.text: Respected politician, say, in presbyter's island

indicators.note: the word for say goes inside the word for presbyter's

parts.note: a presbyter is a church elder, so presbyter's gives elder's
to state is to say
Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Describing a senior politician as if from a church elder's island home.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior figure respected for long experience in government is called by this idiom.

clue.text: Bletherer caught party man on TV

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland
the box is informal for television

explanation.surface: A gossip caught chatting on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party man' is not a politician but Lewis Carroll's Mad Hatter, host of the tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bletherer, from Scottish 'blether', talks idly at length, like a chatterbox.

clue.text: Seasoning don pinched from new town

indicators.note: pinched means stolen, so the word don is taken away from the town

parts.note: Basildon in Essex is one of Britain's post-war planned new towns

explanation.surface: A university don stealing a herb from a modern town.
explanation.walkthrough: BASILDON is a post-war 'new town' in Essex, England; take DON out and the herb remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb used to season food, especially Italian dishes.

clue.text: Commotion made by drunk, mostly, crossing border

indicators.note: crossing means the trimmed word for drunk goes around the word for border
mostly removes the last letter of the word for drunk

parts.note: sozzled is slang for drunk
a hem is a border on fabric

explanation.surface: A drunk causing a disturbance at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a frontier for the drunk to cross, but it is the hem of a garment; the answer is informal, chiefly British, slang for a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A shemozzle is slang for a muddle or rumpus, a commotion.

clue.text: Get the better of Old Bill, taken in by backing of that woman priest

indicators.note: the word for bill is held inside the reversed words for that woman and priest
backing means the words for that woman and priest are run backwards together

parts.note: her refers to that woman
Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend, a priest
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: The police being swindled by a female priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' reads as British slang for the police, but it splits into old and a bill; 'backing of' turns that woman and priest round as one run, VERREH.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach someone is to outwit or cheat them, getting the better of them.

clue.text: Swap truck

definitions.meaning: to trade one thing for another
an old sense meaning barter or dealings

explanation.definitionFit: Exchange means a swap, and truck in its old sense means barter or trade.

clue.text: Hurt, I came out suffering pain

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone emerging hurt and in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, applied to HURT, I and CAME together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rheumatic suffers the aching joints of rheumatism, so is suffering pain.

clue.text: Performance can start to evolve in West

indicators.note: in places the can and the letter inside the name for West

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of evolve

explanation.surface: A show that can begin to develop out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not the direction but Mae West, giving MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film.

clue.text: Public disquiet finally shown after pirate's beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word for pirate is cut off

parts.note: a rover is an old word for a pirate

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of disquiet

explanation.surface: Public unease shown after a pirate's execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is the placing: T comes after OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in public view rather than hidden.

clue.text: Cactus developed in a pot outside university

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for university
developed signals the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cactus grown in a pot at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it is part of the anagram fodder with A POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the genus of prickly-pear cacti.

clue.text: Financial scandal making Channel resort boil?

parts.note: Southsea is a seaside resort near Portsmouth on the English Channel
to bubble is to boil

explanation.surface: A scandal that sets a south-coast town seething.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHSEA is a resort on England's south coast, part of Portsmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Sea Bubble was the 1720 collapse of the South Sea Company's shares, a famous financial scandal.

clue.text: Mountain among hills in Airedale?

indicators.note: among signals the answer lies within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A peak somewhere in the Yorkshire dales.
explanation.walkthrough: Airedale is a valley in Yorkshire, which makes 'hills' look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Stop horse crossing railwa

indicators.note: crossing means the word for horse goes across, around, the railway

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
the print's clipped spelling of railway; EL is the US term for an elevated railway

explanation.surface: Halting a horse at a level crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is the verb: belay is a nautical command to stop. The final word is printed clipped as 'railwa', meaning railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Belay is a command to stop or cease, from its nautical sense of securing a rope.

clue.text: Works by Pindar originally obtained from the French

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of obtained

parts.note: des is French for 'from the' (plural)

explanation.surface: Poems by an ancient Greek poet translated from French.
explanation.walkthrough: Pindar was an ancient Greek lyric poet known for his victory poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Pindar is famous for his odes celebrating athletic victors.

clue.text: A number study outside Australia

indicators.note: outside places the word for study around the word for Australia

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
Oz is informal for Australia

explanation.surface: A count of those who studied outside Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is twelve, a specific number.

clue.text: Hot spot near centre of constable's beat

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of constable's

parts.note: to club is to beat

explanation.surface: A trendy venue near the middle of a policeman's patrol area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a police patrol, but it is the verb, to club.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a lively place of entertainment, such as a nightclub.

clue.text: But surely one doesn't abandon wickedness?

definitions.text: But surely one doesn't abandon wickedness?

parts.words: But surely one doesn't abandon wickedness?
parts.note: split differently the answer reads as 'cast off evil', yet a wicked woman of this kind is the last to give up her wickedness

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about whether someone really gives up sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Split three-five the other way, the answer looks like an instruction to give up wickedness, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a malicious, wicked woman, unlikely to renounce evil.

clue.text: Air passage cat required to cross Arkansas

indicators.note: the word for cat goes across, around, the abbreviation for Arkansas

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat
AR is the US postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: A cat needing an air route over a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air passage' suggests a flight, but it is the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the part of the windpipe housing the vocal cords, an air passage.
